prompt: Write a poem about the sea. Output only the poem, with no title.
raw:
All night the sea turns pebbles in its sleep.
By dawn the green glass of a bottle’s neck
is smooth enough to hold against your cheek.
A little of the cold stays on your skin.

Out past the buoys a fishing boat comes in.
Its engine cuts. For half a minute more
the gulls hang crying in the place it was,
then fold their wings and settle on the swell.
